title: Entanglement entropy in two-particle Grover walks on graphs
authors: Sho Kubota, Haruhiko Matsubara, Etsuo Segawa
abstract: We define a two-particle quantum walk of identical particles on a graph $G$ via the one-particle Grover walk on the Kronecker product $G \otimes G$, and call it the two-particle Grover walk. In systems of identical particles, quantum mechanics requires that quantum states have a certain invariance with respect to the exchange of particles. Focusing on the symmetry of the Kronecker product $G \otimes G$ as a graph, we show that the time evolution operator of this walk commutes with the swap operator, which ensures that this requirement is satisfied. Furthermore, we study the entanglement entropy of quantum states evolved by this walk. For the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, we completely determine the values of $n$ for which the quantum states evolved from specific initial states attain the upper bound of the entropy at some time, and prove that they are exactly $1$ and $2$.
summary: This paper investigates the entanglement entropy generated by two-particle Grover walks on graphs, modeling the system using the Kronecker product structure. The authors prove that for complete bipartite graphs $K_{n,n}$, maximal entanglement is only achieved when $n=1$ or $n=2$. This work provides deep insights into how graph topology constrains quantum information dynamics.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the entanglement entropy of quantum states evolving under a two-particle Grover walk defined on an arbitrary graph G.
main_result: For complete bipartite graphs $K_{n,n}$, the entanglement entropy attains its upper bound if and only if $n=1$ or $n=2$.
method: The analysis relies on analyzing the commutation of the time evolution operator with the swap operator and using spectral properties derived from the amplitude matrix $\Psi$ to check for maximum entanglement.
model_or_system: The model is a two-particle quantum walk defined by extending the one-particle Grover walk onto the Kronecker product graph $G \otimes G$. The system must respect particle indistinguishability, which requires the evolution operator to commute with the swap operator.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy $S(\psi)$ of the two-particle quantum state $\psi$, and whether this entropy reaches its theoretical upper bound ($\log |A(G)|$).
important_parameters: The graph structure (e.g., $K_{n,n}$), the size parameter $n$, and the time step $	au$ are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes simple, finite graphs and focuses heavily on the specific algebraic structure provided by the Kronecker product for defining the walk operator.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the action of the single-particle time evolution operator $U$ and its adjoint $U^*$ on basis states before and after evolution.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the symmetry properties (commutativity with the swap operator) ensuring physical consistency. It then defines the entanglement entropy in terms of the amplitude matrix $\Psi$. Finally, it applies these tools to compute the entropy for specific graph families like $K_{n,n}$ to determine when the upper bound is met.
why_interesting: This work connects quantum walk dynamics (a topic relevant to quantum computation and transport) with entanglement measures. Understanding when maximal entanglement occurs provides insight into the information processing capacity or coherence properties of these quantum systems.
